# Satellite imagery — Style Prompt

> A place seen from far above, graded down to an analyst's grey, with thin white measurement lines drawn on the ground: a lock-on reticle, dashed outlines of what used to be, a ticked range line, one amber reading. One continuous zoom built from nested imagery plates carries the viewer from orbit to the ground, and time runs inside one locked frame by scan bands. True colour comes back only where the story turns.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

- **The ground is imagery, the lines are measurement.** Two layers, two truths: what the satellite saw (soft, grey, grainy) and what the analyst measured (white hairlines, sparse, on real coordinates). Nothing on the ground is decorated.
- **Scale is the camera.** One log-space zoom from orbit to the ground through nested plates (wide, region, detail) that dissolve in with feathered edges; an altitude readout and a scale bar come from the same camera.
- **One finding per screen**, in the single accent colour (the reading).
- **Time is a step on one place.** The year changes, the water drops to the next outline, one amber percentage steps down, and each past shoreline stays as a thin pale ring: the rings stack up as the water shrinks. The exposed lake bed is pale salt with bright edges against dark mid-grey terrain.
- **Colour is evidence**: orbit in true colour, the analysis in grey, colour back only on the subject that changed.
- Not a chart on paper, not a glowing sci-fi HUD (no invented chrome), not a blueprint, not an isometric diorama, not a slide deck.
- The imagery here is drawn, not photographed (a made-up place): say so in a small credit line, and when the user has real imagery or their own survey, it replaces the drawn plates.

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Plates**: three nested rasters painted once at load from one seeded terrain function (wide 640×360 with orbit haze, mid 1024×576, detail 1280×720; each only adds finer octaves, so they match in tone). Mid-grey mottled terrain with dark dry-riverbed veins and grain; the lake is vector water (SVG) over a pale salt bed drawn into the plates from per-angle shoreline radii per year and then only scaled. All three share the same radius table, so every shoreline lines up at every scale.
- **Grade**: grey ramp from `--latar` to `--teks`, never reaching full white (white belongs to the marks). Sea 4–30 %, land 30–70 %, a faint foam band along the coast.
- **Marks**: SVG hairlines 2.2 px with a 5.4 px halo in `--latar` at 84 %, constant width at any zoom (`vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`); dashes for history (14/9) and claims (4/6), solid for the measured outline. Brackets, ticks, leader lines.
- **Scan band**: a soft gradient 120 px tall, brighter at its leading edge, never a hairline.
- **Post**: static film grain at about 55 % opacity and a vignette. No blur on moving plates.

## 3. Colour logic

| Role | Token |
|---|---|
| Ground (sea, shadow, halo) | `--latar` |
| Land, marks, text on the ground | `--teks` (imagery is the ramp `--latar` → `--teks`) |
| The single reading, the contact | `--utama-di-latar` |
| A second hue for a claim layer (a plan, a map), flat | `--aksen-di-latar` |
| Fixed, belong to the look | orbit blue-grey sea and olive land, the green of regrowth (`--hijau`) |

White means measured. Amber is never decoration: one reading on screen at a time. Text over imagery always carries a halo in `--latar`; dark brands read as the film, pale brands as its negative with dark marks.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul` (Oswald 500): the reading (150 px at 1920 wide, units 54 px) and the closing title (128 px, uppercase).
- `--font-isi` (Inter 600/400): labels (24 px uppercase, tracking 0.06 em), the transcript strip (34 px), notes (24 px). Nothing under 20 px.
- IBM Plex Mono: instruments and dates (altitude 34 px, date stamp 74 px, credit 20 px, coordinates 24 px).
- Labels attach to the ground with a leader line; the reading sits in the right third beside what it measures: label above, note below.
- Transcript strip bottom-left: a 2 px white rule, a dark plate fading to the right, each cue on one line.

## 5. Motion quality

- The camera never stops: the dive is an ease-in-out cubic over 3.6 s from 1/12 to 1 (log space) with a 7° rotation unwinding; afterwards a 5 % creep over the next 8 s.
- Marks arrive by being made: lines reveal top to bottom (0.5–1 s), ticks fade in staggered at 0.13 s, a counter rolls over 1.1 s and lands with a small pop, the reticle searches with a wander of ±210 px then snaps with a 10 px overshoot (decay `e^(−9t)`).
- Scan band 0.7 s per swap; date spacing 1.4–1.7 s; the stamp changes mid-scan.
- Colour returns over 1 s, `power1.inOut`, only on the subject.
- Never moves: instruments, strip, the ground under its annotations.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Orbit dive (log zoom, slight rotation) | scale, going to look | an opening; locating anything |
| Locked nadir frame, slow creep | evidence, comparison | time running in one place |
| Push-in on a point | singling out | one site, one structure |
| Track along a line | distance | a river, a road, a border |
| Whip pan | meanwhile, a counter-example | a second place at the same altitude |
| Climb back to orbit | consequence, perspective | an ending |

Transitions: scan-band swaps, plate dissolves while zooming, the reticle opening into a card. No crossfades between unrelated places.

## 7. Native moves

- **The dive.** Orbit in true colour, a reticle wanders, locks, the plates sharpen under it. *Fits content like:* a village profile, a class on geography, a developer's site, a logistics route.
- **Time in a locked frame.** Dated plates scan in; each leaves its outline (dashed history, solid latest). *Fits content like:* a reforestation project, a city's growth, a farm's season, a reservoir refilling.
- **The range line.** Two marks, a ticked line grows from one to the other while the reading counts up and lands. *Fits content like:* how far a shore moved, a delivery radius, a trail's length, a school's catchment.
- **Colour returns where the story turns.** Only the subject regains true colour inside the grey. *Fits content like:* regrown mangroves, an irrigated field, a cleaned river, a new park.
- **The reticle becomes the frame.** Lock brackets open out around the closing card. *Fits content like:* a campaign call to action, a report title, a tour booking, a channel intro.

## 8. Pitfalls

- Marks that fight the ground: keep lines thin, white, sparse, with the halo; one reading at a time.
- Crossfading plates without a scan: time changes are bands, not dissolves.
- Letting the camera freeze: always a creep, no still longer than a second.
- Colour everywhere: if everything is green, nothing turned.
- Labels floating off the ground: every label has a leader to a coordinate.
- Painting at load is the cost: keep the plates small (≤ 960×540), paint once, move as images.
- Presenting drawn imagery as evidence: keep the credit line; real imagery needs its licence and credit burned in.

# Satellite imagery: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 2, medium 3, long 4.2.

## hook

- en: high-altitude haze over mid-grey terrain, the place title over it; the altitude readout ticks down as the one continuous push-in begins
- id: kabut dari ketinggian di atas medan abu-abu, judul tempat di atasnya; angka ketinggian turun saat satu dorongan kamera terus-menerus dimulai

## problem

- en: locked nadir frame, slow creep: the old outline prints as a dashed hairline and the dated plate shows what is wrong
- id: bingkai tegak terkunci, merayap pelan: garis tepi lama tercetak putus-putus dan citra bertanggal menunjukkan masalahnya

## fact

- en: a soft scan band swaps the plate for the next date, north to south; each date leaves its outline and the date stamp changes
- id: pita pindai lembut mengganti citra ke tanggal berikutnya, utara ke selatan; tiap tanggal meninggalkan garis tepi, stempel berganti

## step

- en: one year per step: the water drops to its next outline, the year flips, the amber % steps down, each old shoreline stays as a pale ring
- id: satu tahun per langkah: air turun ke garis berikutnya, tahun berganti, persen kuning turun, tepi lama tertinggal jadi cincin pucat

## compare

- en: two dated plates of one frame, a scan band wiping the later over the earlier; both outlines stay printed for the eye
- id: dua citra bertanggal dari satu bingkai, pita pindai menyapu yang baru di atas yang lama; kedua garis tepi tetap tercetak

## number

- en: a ticked range line grows between two marks while one amber reading counts up and lands; true colour returns on the subject only
- id: garis jarak bertanda tumbuh sementara satu bacaan kuning menghitung naik lalu mendarat; warna asli kembali hanya di subjek

## proof

- en: close view at the end of the push-in: dashed outline of the oldest shoreline, the stacked rings, one place label on a leader line
- id: pandangan dekat di ujung dorongan kamera: garis tepi tertua putus-putus, cincin bertumpuk, satu label tempat pada garis penunjuk

## offer

- en: the reticle snaps onto the subject with a small overshoot and a label leader names it; the offer is read in one line beside it
- id: pembidik mengunci subjek dengan sedikit memantul dan garis penunjuk menamainya; tawarannya dibaca satu baris di sampingnya

## cta

- en: the lock brackets open out into a frame around the closing card over the dimmed ground; held 2 s
- id: kurung pembidik membuka menjadi bingkai kartu penutup di atas tanah yang diredupkan; diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: climb back out: the zoom reverses to the wide plate while the last reading holds; the frame closes on the title; held 2 s
- id: naik kembali: zoom berbalik ke citra lebar sementara bacaan terakhir bertahan; bingkai menutup pada judul; diam 2 detik

      const RR = PCT.map(() => []);
      function rings() { // tepi bersarang: tiap tahun lebih kecil dari yang sebelumnya

      function plate(W, H, span, res, o = {}) {
